source: known difference: #282, ph1-quirks: the oracle writes the cells through KeepingRecord, as word_edit_table's set_cells does (docx-agent's _Kept): a cell written inside the placed block takes its column out of the table's record (customXml/item1.xml); docx-agent's document-level set_cells, this mode's reference, writes the same cells and leaves the record saying they hold the source's values. Our record contract, which Word does not read; the tool-level set_cells on these tables is compared in the objects mode, without differences.

known difference: #282: /result/removed. The Rust core reports the row removed outright and its two paragraphs (tr:5B0000B0, p:5B0000AE, p:5B0000AF), none of which the document has after the edit; docx-agent's delete_block names a gone row's paragraphs by id() of their lxml proxies taken before the deletion, and the detached row's paragraphs come back as new proxies, so only the row is named. A docx-agent leftover (the paragraphs are gone, as an untracked deletion reports), not copied.

known difference: docx-agent's insert_control takes the position unchecked and fails inside new_run with Python's IndexError ('list index out of range', not_found); the Rust core refuses the position, saying how many characters the paragraph has (as word_notes refuses one). A docx-agent crash, not copied.
